chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is obligatory for the believer upon the believer that he advises him.
ai.seo_question: What is the obligation of a believer towards another believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s Chapter 90, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates nasihah from a general virtue to a specific, binding obligation (wajib) between believers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on communal solidarity and spiritual accountability. This mutual duty ensures that the community maintains both doctrinal purity and moral integrity through constructive correction. It underscores the relational nature of faith, where each believer acts as a guardian for the spiritual well-being of the other.
